description: Verify that DUT-emitted UDP with odd payload size carries a valid Internet checksum, with proper pseudo-header zero-pad processing for the trailing odd byte (RFC 768 'Fields' MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
UDP checksums are computed over the pseudo-header + UDP header + payload, with a trailing zero byte appended if the data length is odd. This is a frequent bug surface — naive implementations forget the pad, producing a wrong checksum on odd-length payloads.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: OpTriggerSendUdp request with odd-length payload

2. Observation:
   • DUT → Tester: UDP datagram
     - checksum verifies against (pseudo-header + UDP header + payload + 0-pad)   ← key check

[Pass condition]
DUT-emitted UDP checksum is valid for the odd-length payload.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_invalid_checksum — DUT emitted UDP with checksum that does not validate (likely missing the zero-pad in the cksum computation)
• Fail_timeout — DUT did not emit any UDP within the listen window

verdicts.Pass: DUT-emitted odd-payload UDP carries valid checksum — normal
verdicts.Fail_invalid_checksum: DUT emitted UDP with invalid pseudo-header checksum on odd payload
verdicts.Fail_timeout: No DUT-originated UDP within the listen window
